justifications.layering: Sources are only read in staging, everything uses ref(), and shared logic is pulled into macros (clean_raw, dedupe, recent_races_filter). But the dependency direction is inverted in places: int_f1__driver_profiles reads fct_results, fct_session_results and mart_driver_season_standings, and int_f1__teammate_pace_deltas reads fct_driver_race_pace and fct_results. Some logic is also duplicated: the 60 s red-flag cut-off is written separately in mart_constructor_season_pit_stops, int_f1__circuit_season_pit_stops and mart_pit_stop_trend_by_season (where it is a bare literal 60000), and fct_stints re-implements the recent_races_filter lookback inline instead of calling the macro.
justifications.naming: Prefixes are consistent (stg_f1__, int_f1__, fct_/dim_/mart_), columns are snake_case with units in the name (lap_time_ms, duration_ms, median_pit_stop_seconds), and each layer has its own YAML (_f1__sources.yml, _f1__models.yml, _int_f1__models.yml, _marts__models.yml, separate *_unit_tests.yml). Small issues: the line between fct_ and mart_ is loose (fct_driver_race_pace is really an aggregate, while the crosswalks are named dim_), the 1,080-line _marts__models.yml is hard to navigate, and the README's macros line lists only clean_raw and time_text_to_ms.
justifications.testing: Coverage is strong and at the right layers. Source tests guard schema and format (source_columns_missing/added, matches_regex), which would catch the task-5 vendor migration (lap_times renamed to lap_timing, DD/MM/YYYY dates). Duplicate tests (duplicate_key_rows, no_conflicting_duplicates) plus assert_facts_conserve_staging_rows would catch the task-6 duplicated constructor and standings rows. Business rules are tested at the marts (assert_champions_match_history against a seed, incomplete seasons, antisymmetry), and unit tests cover parsing, stints, countback and placeholders. Weak spots: the relationships test from stg_f1__results to int_f1__drivers_with_placeholders passes by construction; assert_pit_stops_exclude_red_flags only checks that the median is under 60 s, which is nearly vacuous; and fct_telemetry uniqueness is checked only on the latest batch by default.
justifications.quirks: Every quirk is handled on purpose and explained in a comment or description: `\N` and empty strings via clean_raw; m:ss.mmm text via time_text_to_ms, with pit stop DURATION skipped in favour of milliseconds (stg_f1__pit_stops); red-flag stops over 60 s; sprints split out in fct_session_results, with official sprint points kept in the standings; pre-1991 dropped scores handled by taking official standings rather than summed points (README, mart_driver_season_standings); shared drives counted with count(distinct race_id) in int_f1__driver_profiles; incomplete seasons via int_f1__season_status; late-arriving drivers via int_f1__drivers_with_placeholders and mart_orphan_driver_results; and lapped finishers recovered from POSITIONTEXT in the finish_position macro.
justifications.incremental_snapshot: fct_lap_times and fct_stints use delete+insert on race_id with a two-race lookback, so a reissued race fully replaces its old rows (including deleted laps) and reruns are idempotent. fct_telemetry tracks a loaded_at watermark with a lookback in hours and reloads affected races whole; the README notes that a correction with no new delivery needs a full refresh. The check strategy in snp_drivers suits a table with no updated_at column, but it snapshots raw, un-deduplicated source text. The task-6 duplicate-driver problem would break its unique_key, and history records `\N` text instead of typed nulls.
justifications.change_hygiene: Each ticket is one coherent commit, and the README is extended to match: vendor migration, quality gates, interfaces, the Vendor B crosswalk, telemetry, CI and analysis. Fixes landed where they belong (staging dedupe, identifier: mapping for the renamed table), and there is no commented-out or dead code. Some later work was bolted on rather than refactored: fct_stints copies the lookback logic, the pit-stop threshold was copied into the new trend models instead of being centralised, and the README's macro list was never updated.
justifications.docs: Descriptions cover every mart column, and the model header comments explain the reasoning, for example why stop DURATION is ignored, why standings are not summed race points, how the crosswalk scores and resolves ties, the telemetry pruning trade-off in fct_telemetry, and leave-one-out teammate adjustment in mart_driver_teammate_performance. The README is a real onboarding guide. The only nit is the gendered 'his' in some descriptions.
justifications.interfaces: The f1_analytics group is defined in _groups.yml, fct_results and dim_drivers are access: public, every mart has an enforced contract, dim_drivers is versioned with latest_version: 2 and a v1 deprecation_date (both built from int_f1__driver_profiles so their numbers cannot drift), and a semantic layer with metrics sits on fct_results. The weak part is the version unit tests in _marts__dim_drivers_unit_tests.yml: they only check that columns pass through. Several protected marts also leave access implicit instead of declaring it.
justifications.open_ended: docs/analysis/leadership-questions.md and its marts give defensible definitions. 'Overperforming the car' is measured against the same-car teammate (deepest common qualifying session plus green-flag race pace), adjusted for teammate strength with leave-one-out, with uncertainty across driver-season stints and an explicit insufficient_data verdict. The pit-stop question uses a chain-linked index that controls for circuit mix. The write-up pushes back where the questions mislead (the car dominates, ratings are relative and zero-sum within a team, pit-lane time is not stationary time) and lists the data limits.

biggest_strength: Data quirks and vendor risk are handled deliberately and defensively. Source schema, format and duplicate gates, row-conservation tests and a champions-vs-history test would stop the task 5 and 6 failures before they reach a mart, and the docs consistently explain why each rule exists.
biggest_weakness: Layering is not clean: intermediate models depend on marts (int_f1__driver_profiles, int_f1__teammate_pace_deltas), and some business rules are copied rather than shared (the 60 s red-flag cut-off in three models, the race lookback re-implemented in fct_stints). On top of that, snp_drivers snapshots raw, un-deduplicated source text, which the known duplicate-driver issue would break.
